experience.title: Founder & Software Engineer
bullets: Founded Apex Freight Capital, a freight brokerage for steel, oversized equipment and infrastructure loads, and built its in-house software in Python, TypeScript and Docker instead of buying a brokerage platform.

Built the AI Gmail Manager (Python, scikit-learn, SQLite) that classifies freight, quote and carrier email, learns priorities from starred messages and answers questions about the inbox, cutting daily email triage from about 90 minutes to 25.

Built AI Jarvis 2.0, the company's AI command center, with agent routing, task queues and a human approval step before anything reaches a customer or carrier, plus provider switching across OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek, usage tracking and health monitoring.

Built a containerized RAG API (FastAPI, ChromaDB, Ollama) that answers questions over company documents such as rate confirmations, carrier packets, permit rules and operating procedures, with Swagger docs and GitHub Actions CI/CD.

Self-hosted DeepSeek-Coder on rented Vast.ai GPUs behind FastAPI and Gradio as a private coding assistant, with a Docker image and idempotent bootstrap that rebuild a destroyed instance and serve again in under 5 minutes.

Built Mozart Dueling AI to review the company's own code before release: it sends the same code to GPT-4 and DeepSeek, scores both reviews on 11 criteria including correctness, security, error handling and test coverage, and picks the stronger answer.

Built Python lead research that normalizes government award records and resolves recipients to companies through entity matching, keeping the source behind every signal, to find infrastructure projects that will need heavy freight.

experience.title: AI Evaluation Contributor, Software Engineering
bullets: Contributed to AI training and technical evaluation work, including a Snorkel-related guest project: rated model responses on code- and reasoning-focused tasks against the project guidelines and wrote the evidence-based rationale behind every rating.

Evaluated model-written code and technical answers for correctness, instruction following and completeness, reproducing each proposed fix in a clean environment and checking its claims against documentation, edge cases and the failing test it claimed to resolve.

Reviewed multi-step coding-agent trajectories in Cursor and Claude Code (diffs, tool calls, terminal output, tests and logs) and documented where a solution passed the visible tests yet missed the stated requirement, a boundary input or an error path.

Classified failures in model output by type (logic error, unhandled edge case, security gap, missing error handling, tests that do not prove the fix) and turned each into actionable corrective feedback.
